# Add minimal browser support

## Pull Request by @tomusdrw

Related: #443 (compatibility on `env` and `measure` is good enough for now)
Related: #407 (just exposing importer suffice, however running full node with proper `importBlock` API is desired)

This PR exposes `importer` via `@typeberry/lib` and makes sure that the whole API is usable in browser.

It isn't an ideal API for running the entire node in the browser yet, but it's a start.

The example usage of this API will be visible in `state-viewer` where a STF vector will be executed directly in the browser so that we can easily inspec any potential state differences between the expected post state and the one we get from execution.

## Walkthrough

This PR adds bin/jam and bin/lib package entries and re-exports (`@typeberry/importer`, `@typeberry/workers-api`) from bin/lib, introduces DbHeaderChain and threads a HeaderChain into OnChain and related call sites, reshapes the codec module surface (namespace ↦ top-level descriptors and many consumers switched to codec.*), centralizes environment access via packages/core/utils/env.ts, adds async/static factories (TransitionHasher.create, InMemorySerializedStates.new/withHasher), and updates worker/port APIs (threadId, eventemitter3) plus numerous import-path and test adjustments.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~60 minutes

Areas needing extra attention:
- packages/core/codec/descriptors.ts and public codec re-exports (semantic API surface changes)
- packages/jam/transition/chain-stf.ts and all OnChain call sites (DbHeaderChain/headerChain plumbing)
- packages/jam/transition/hasher.ts and packages/jam/database/serialized-states-db.ts (new async/static factories and hasher wiring)
- Worker API surface: packages/workers/api/port.ts, api-node, and packages/workers/api/config.ts (threadId, EventEmitter swap, generics)
- Widespread import-path migrations to codec-utils and codec namespace usages (ensure no mixed imports remain)

The `@typeberry/utils` package re-exports test utilities (`test.ts`) that have a top-level `import assert from "node:assert"` at module level. ## Comment by @coderabbitai[bot]

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**fixedLength=0 in `dictionary` leads to mismatched encode/decode**

In `dictionary`, the length‑prefix behavior for fixed‑length dictionaries has an edge‑case bug:

```ts
// encode
if (fixedLength === undefined || fixedLength === 0) {
  e.varU32(tryAsU32(data.length));
}

// decode
const len = fixedLength ?? d.varU32();
```

If `fixedLength === 0`, encoding writes a varU32 length prefix, but decoding will always take `len = fixedLength` (i.e. 0) and **will not** read the prefix. That desynchronizes the decoder (it leaves the length word in the stream) and breaks decoding.

If `fixedLength` is meant to mean “no prefix, always exactly N entries”, the encoder condition should treat only `undefined` as “variable length”:

```diff
-      // length prefix
-      if (fixedLength === undefined || fixedLength === 0) {
-        e.varU32(tryAsU32(data.length));
-      }
+      // length prefix only for variable-length dictionaries
+      if (fixedLength === undefined) {
+        e.varU32(tryAsU32(data.length));
+      }
```

This keeps the current behavior for `fixedLength === undefined` and makes `fixedLength === 0` a truly fixed‑length (empty) dictionary without a redundant prefix, matching the decode path.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In packages/core/codec/descriptors.ts around lines 313 to 384, the encoder
currently writes a length prefix when fixedLength === 0 (condition: fixedLength
=== undefined || fixedLength === 0) while the decoder treats fixedLength === 0
as a fixed-length empty dictionary and does not read a prefix, causing stream
desync; change the encoder to only write the varU32 length prefix when
fixedLength === undefined (remove the fixedLength === 0 branch) so encoding and
decoding agree that fixedLength === 0 is a true fixed-length (empty) dictionary.
```

</details>
